text.cell: Each cell: spent less the vote that year. Shaded by how far, against the vote.
text.ledger_note: From the school journal, every line tied to the Town’s year-end report.
text.no_restart: FY2023: no restarted-high count. FY2022 is in the workbook, not the journal, and a flag reads one record.
text.none: not on this account that year
text.open_year: Open the year in the FY breakdown
text.scroll: More years: scroll the table sideways
text.sort: Sorted by the size of its misses, all years together; click a heading to sort
text.usual_note: Usual year: the median of a line’s years, spent against its vote. A line usually misses one way when that median is 10% or more over or under budget (and at least $5,000), or $50,000 or more either way, over 3 or more years. Thresholds of ours.
text.workbook_note: FY2018 to FY2022: the Finance Committee’s workbook, built from MUNIS exports a year at a time. Assembled by a person, so stated, not proof. Read against the journal where both exist, it gives the same vote, transfers, final budget and spending on every line: 269 lines in FY2023 and 264 lines in FY2024.
text.workbook_restart: In the workbook years, last year’s spending is after re-charges to other funds: the workbook cannot show them. From FY2024 it is before them.

so.text: A line flagged year after year is a pattern in how it is budgeted; one flagged once is a year’s event, and that year’s FY breakdown shows what moved.

blocks.title: Each line, year by year

paragraphs.text: **The budget documents** print a budget and an actual column the district wrote. Lines are read with the rules of the August analysis: a line under $10,000, a cell two documents disagree about, and FY2021 are not counted: that year the documents print the budget in the actual column. The dot chart reads them, and FY2021 from the workbook.

**The Finance Committee workbook** pastes per-year MUNIS exports side by side, by account, with transfers. A person assembled it, so it is stated, not proof; in FY2023 and FY2024 it equals the journal on every line. The grid reads it before FY2023.
**The school journal** is the Town’s own accounting record, and every line here ties to its year-end report. It also records re-charges to other funds, which the workbook does not.
**They are never added together.** A line-year is read from one record only.

note.text: Private and collaborative tuition: above zero, spent over budget; below, under. The documents, then the journal from FY2023.

so.text: A salary vote leaves room the year usually does not use; that room is where a surplus starts. Why, post by post, the books do not say.

conclusions.text: Salary lines came in under their vote in 4 of 4 journal years; the documents agree, at 0.80% under budget.

so.text: Most lines miss both ways and cancel; the few that lean one way are where a vote and its line part company year after year.

conclusions.text: 24 of 288 lines usually miss one way, FY2018–FY2026: 15 over budget, 9 under.

so.text: No trend to project: the site’s projection holds this line flat rather than growing it at a rate.

conclusions.text: Out-of-district tuition ran from 27.0% over budget to 51.5% under budget, FY2018–FY2026.

so.text: Each is a question for the next budget: was the cut a one-year saving, or a line set high?

conclusions.text: 51 of 163 times a line gave budget up mid-year, its next vote was 10% or more above its spending.

finding.text: School lines land near their vote in total every year, and far from it one by one, in both directions.

not_established: Why any line was voted above or below what it spent: a vacancy, a placement, a price change and a plan all produce the same figures.
